title.narrative: NICFI 26-28 SEI - Trase: Intelligence for sustainable trade

description.narrative:
The project is implemented by Stockholm Environment Institute, jointly led by Global-Canopy, Trase co-founder. Sub-grantees receiving Norad funds are Yayasan Auriga Nusantara, and Instituto Centro de Vida.
The project will provide open data and intelligence on global trade, consumption of forest risk commodities to be used in policy development and implementation, as well as technical support and guidance to build capacity of CSOs, governments and businesses to apply risk-based approaches in supply chain policies and interventions.
Impact: The delivery of supply chain commitments and policies by governments and businesses is accelerated to effectively reduce deforestation and other environmental and social impacts, while opportunities to scale ambition and increase responsiveness to changing risks and opportunities are strengthened
Outcomes: - By December 2028, more than 25% of the domestic and international trade in commodities linked to deforestation and conversion is regulated by a combination of government policies and voluntary private sector initiatives in consumer and producer market - By December 2028, at least 20 governments, businesses, CSOs and donors shift their agendas by increasing attention to new or emerging risks, limits and opportunities in supply chain sustainability, including through public reactions and changes in resource allocation, where additional or changed agenda - By December 2028, at least 25 media campaigns and/or strategic litigation efforts prioritize and align scrutiny of governments and businesses to ensure the delivery of existing supply chain sustainability commitments, address gapsin coverage and/or address the unintended consequences of these measures. - More than 60 third-party organizations to support governments and businesses to more effectively design, implement and improve supply chain policies and interventions that target the impacts of forest risk commodities on forests, nature and people
